scope.method: Read all 250 displayed models; separately recalculate every primary result in SI or compatible declared units; inspect mechanism/verification text for physical interpretation and all flagged cases.
scope.limits: Educational arithmetic, dimensional and physical-boundary review. Not source-project data validation, code compliance, equipment operating authorization, site design verification or professional certification.

courseBoundaryReview.b151: Closed-ring membrane estimate is conditional on contact; voids induce bending. Early-age strength, rebound, bond, thickness minima and strain-zero/temperature history are separate evidence.
courseBoundaryReview.b152: Panel energy and residual ratios remain test-geometry dependent; bending resistance uses the rectangular elastic section modulus. No conversion of panel energy to tunnel-system energy.
courseBoundaryReview.b153: Two equal vertical bolts require symmetric load sharing. Steel, bond and plate bearing capacities are distinct; pull test reaction and local interface do not certify a whole wedge.
courseBoundaryReview.b154: N=pRs is the complete uniform-pressure ring idealization. Euler uses effective elastic straight-column length, not proof of curved-rib capacity. Joints and lateral restraint remain independent.
courseBoundaryReview.b155: Pipe umbrella needs forward ground and rear support. Simple-span moment, intact-tube inertia and local Winkler line support are comparison models; joint rotation must distinguish local chord slope from two-sided relative rotation.
courseBoundaryReview.b156: Tributary area is geometrical, not uniform bar-force allocation. Bond maturity, retained embedment and three-dimensional deviation govern reinforcement continuity.
courseBoundaryReview.b157: Membrane blocks flow but does not replace lining pressure resistance. P/T requires absolute pressure/temperature and fixed gas volume/mass. Completeness percentages are not reliability.
courseBoundaryReview.b158: Hydrostatic fresh-concrete pressure is a reference envelope. L^4 scaling holds fixed line load, EI and supports; full-restraint thermal stress ignores creep/slip and is an ideal upper comparison.
courseBoundaryReview.b159: N=pR assumes a closed ring; not an open invert. Coulomb resistance is an isolated assumed interface. Uniform head-area uplift is separate from bearing, early-age wheel loads and leaking-head changes.
courseBoundaryReview.b160: Stored elastic, projectile, drop-weight and component work are different energies. Static serial-force minimum does not predict dynamic system energy; remaining constant-force work requires verified residual travel.
courseBoundaryReview.b161: Stress-strength ratio is screening, not a squeeze prediction. Installation displacement changes support engagement. Summed sliding-joint shortening is circumferential, not diametral closure. Calibration does not prove parameter identifiability.
courseBoundaryReview.b162: Free swelling and constrained swelling pressure cannot be proportionally converted. Strain-times-thickness is a uniform layer idealization. Drawdown effective-stress increment isolates the pore-pressure component.
courseBoundaryReview.b163: Pressure datum/elevation, fluid density and flowing line losses are distinct. Parallel-plate cubic law needs laminar fixed-gradient assumptions; connected void volume is not a grout-take instruction.
courseBoundaryReview.b164: Storage balance assumes steady storage. Manning needs hydraulic slope and compatible geometry; D^(8/3) requires geometrically similar effective circular passages. Pump redundancy may share failure modes.
courseBoundaryReview.b165: Condensation, structural opening, water head and flow-path diversion are separate. Conductance comparisons need matched flow law; chloride mass is exposure, not predicted corrosion penetration.
courseBoundaryReview.b166: Construction stages change both load path and flotation resistance. Raw weight/uplift ratio is not a code factor. Settlement slope, rigid tilt, distortion and standard survey uncertainty must not be conflated.
courseBoundaryReview.b167: Early slab stiffness and column effective length use construction states. Drawdown increases effective stress only as an isolated pore-pressure change; excavation unloading must be superposed separately.
courseBoundaryReview.b168: Tonnes are mass. Displacement balance is not stability; GM requires free-surface correction. Hydrostatic bulkhead resultant uses the stated triangular pressure geometry. Drag excludes wave/acceleration dynamics; land simple-span bending is not a floating beam model.
courseBoundaryReview.b169: Foundation pressure uses net downward force after buoyancy. Long-term compressibility and partial bed contact differ. One-element chord tilt becomes joint relative rotation only with an explicit adjacent orientation.
courseBoundaryReview.b170: Seal compression and clearance are geometric and do not establish contact force or water tightness. p times span is transverse resultant, not membrane tension. Relative rotation needs both adjacent orientations.
courseBoundaryReview.b171: Rectangular box is a staged frame. A one-metre simple strip is not the entire box; force eccentricity uses stated A and Z. Settlement slope is neither a track-twist acceptance rule nor a damage criterion.
courseBoundaryReview.b172: Density mixture estimates incremental solids relative to specified carrier. Pipe friction is a specified equivalent-Newtonian Darcy model. Gaussian settlement area is per metre and not equal to instantaneous spoil imbalance.
courseBoundaryReview.b173: Intermediate stations require a closed reaction path; front and rear demands are staged, not simultaneously applied to every joint. Uniform axial shortening excludes nonlinear joint compression. Curvature resultant assumes equal axial forces on both sides.
courseBoundaryReview.b174: Projection and radius depend on angle units and segment definitions. Heading drift example is geometrical amplification of a stated angle, not a time-integrated path. Utility radii remain to be deducted. Steel strain example does not transfer to plastics.
courseBoundaryReview.b175: Static force imbalance cannot predict sinking speed. Upward flow reduces effective stress; critical gradient is ideal saturated granular soil, not undrained clay uplift. Plug self-weight alone does not establish wall transfer or permanent flotation safety.

findings.issue: Initial stress and early-age strength lacked explicit input units.
findings.resolution: Both inputs now explicitly MPa; 0.50 and 0.75 remain correct.

findings.issue: One measured chord slope was labeled relative joint rotation.
findings.resolution: Now apparentChordRotation; one gauge cannot determine relative joint rotation without both sides.

findings.issue: Fourth-power span sensitivity needed the fixed line-load/stiffness/support assumptions.
findings.resolution: Now fixes uniform q, EI and simple supports; ratio 1.4641 unchanged.

findings.issue: Summed tangential joint travel needed circumferential versus diametral distinction.
findings.resolution: Now circumferentialShortening, explicitly not diametral convergence.

findings.issue: Ten-metre hydrostatic correction implied water density in a grout course.
findings.resolution: Now conveyed-fluid density 1000 kg/m3 and instruction to recalculate for other grout density.

findings.issue: D^(8/3) scaling needed geometrically similar effective circular passages.
findings.resolution: Now explicitly full circular passages, same energy slope and roughness, not arbitrary deposition geometry.

findings.issue: Settlement slope was not distinguished from structural distortion with rigid tilt removed.
findings.resolution: Now meanSettlementSlope with explicit rigid-body tilt not removed. Definition clarification, not an arithmetic correction.

findings.issue: RSS of independent standard uncertainties was called a survey closure residual.
findings.resolution: Now combinedStandardUncertainty and explicitly not a measured closure residual.

findings.issue: One element chord slope needed the adjacent orientation before interpreting joint rotation.
findings.resolution: Now chordInclination plus explicit rigid-element and horizontal-neighbor condition.

findings.issue: Relative joint rotation and opening difference needed explicit adjacent-element orientation.
findings.resolution: Now rigid element beside a horizontal neighbor; 0.001 m opening difference remains correct.

findings.issue: Rail settlement slope needed distinction from distortion and track twist.
findings.resolution: Now meanSettlementSlope with rigid tilt not removed and not track twist.

findings.issue: Final angular drift times full length could be confused with integrated path error.
findings.resolution: Now finalAngleProjection explicitly applies final angle over whole length and excludes time-integrated path interpretation.

additionalReferences.scope: FHWA bridge terminology also uses differential settlement/span as angular distortion; the peer finding requests definition clarity in building/rail contexts, not a claim that the ratio is arithmetically wrong.
